purpose: Adjudicated convention-C comparison sites for scripts/convention-c-value-audit.py. An entry here is the ONLY thing that stops a confirmed convention-C binding from blocking that audit.
why_a_committed_file: The audit reads no names and no comments, by design: its whole premise is that it cannot be evaded by re-spelling, and docs/audits/2026-08-15-detector-blindness-taxonomy.md records sixteen spellings that defeated shape-matching detectors, four of them found BY detectors written to catch the previous blind spot. A '# comparison only' comment or a z_C-style name would be an exemption an author grants themselves inside the file being audited -- the same evasion surface, one level up. A ledger entry cannot be granted that way. It lives outside the scanned tree, it must be committed as a separate deliberate act, and its key includes a hash of the site's own source line, so editing that line expires the adjudication automatically. Same shape as docs/audits/lean-vacuity-review-ledger.json, which holds agent verdicts a machine cannot reach for the same reason.
what_co_binding_is_not: The audit reports which confirmed-C sites are co-bound with a convention-D binding in the same enclosing scope. That is a value-level hint at which sites are PROBABLY comparisons, and it deliberately carries no exemption power: it can be gamed by adding a throwaway z_D beside the site. Co-binding is why a site gets PROPOSED for the ledger (--propose-ledger). It is never why a site is exempt; the commit is.
how_to_add_an_entry: 2. Take the stub for the site you are adjudicating.
3. Fill in `rationale` with why that site binds z_C deliberately -- what it compares, and what would be lost by binding only z_D.
5. Commit it here. Do NOT edit the audited source to make the site disappear; that is AGENTS.md 1a audit-dodging.

6. If the site's source line later changes, the entry stops matching and the site blocks again. That is intended: the adjudication was about that expression, and it is now a different one. The audit lists such entries as `stale` (non-blocking) so they can be pruned or renewed.

entries.rationale: `z_of(q, convention)` is a two-arm frame-comparison helper: the D arm returns the canonical `markov_z(q) = q**3/(q**2+1)`, the C arm returns `sqrt(q)/(q+1)`, and the probe calls both to measure the frame difference in the He-4 body-order shortfall. The function's own docstring scopes the C arm 'excised - computed here ONLY to measure the frame difference, never wired'. Binding only z_D would delete the comparison the probe exists to make. NOTE: --propose-ledger does NOT stub this site, because its D arm is a CALL (`markov_z(q)`) rather than an inline z_D binding, so the co-binding hint does not fire. Adjudicated by hand for that reason; see bean qou-1jny.

entries.source: z_C = 1 / (sp.sqrt(q) + 1 / sp.sqrt(q))   # EXCISED — kept as the comparison arm
entries.rationale: MEASURED, not asserted. This probe's content is a two-sided contrast: it asserts bar(z) = z - h holds for z_D and FAILS for any bar-even z, hence for z_C. z_C is a quantified CANDIDATE here, not a convention the file computes in. Setting z_C := z_D drops the probe from 5/5 to 2/5 -- C_is_coefficient_half_invariant, C_fails_full_bar_condition and verdict_reverses_between_conditions all flip to FAIL. The file itself says this result 'is one of the reasons the ruling reads the way it does', so migrating the site would delete the evidence for the D ruling.

Same shape, symbolic arm. The module docstring states the probe's purpose as 'noting that z_C is bar-invariant where z_D is not' and concludes that z_C's bar-invariance is NOT a tiebreaker in D's favour. The z_C binding is the object that claim is about; the neighbouring z_D_expr is labelled CANONICAL and is what the rank-2 check tests against. Removing or migrating z_C leaves the docstring's claim unevaluable.

The numeric arm of the same comparison as z_C_expr in this file: the symbolic claim is re-checked at q0. Migrating it would make the numeric arm agree with the D arm by construction and the comparison vacuous.

entries.source: z_c = mp.sqrt(q) / (q + 1)                    # convention C, for the comparison only
entries.rationale: The file's own docstring states the contrast it exists to test: 'z_C(1/q)/z_C(q) = 1  bar-even'  vs  'z_D(1/q)/z_D(q) = q^-4  NOT bar-even', and the scope computes bar_ratio_D beside this binding. z_c is the bar-even reference the D ratio is measured against; with it migrated both ratios would be D's and the bar-parity contrast would vanish.
